ai.description: *Chrysopelea taprobanica* reaches 60–90 cm. It is yellowish-green with black-edged scales and red vertebral spots. It is distinguished by its ability to glide and a distinct black-and-yellow head pattern.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Chrysopelea taprobanica* is best distinguished by its unique dorsal pattern of distinct, reddish-orange or yellowish crossbars that lack the black-bordered scales of *C. ornata*.
ai.habitat: *Chrysopelea taprobanica* inhabits dry-zone tropical forests and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low to moderate elevations below 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Sri Lankan flying snake is primarily diurnal, using its ability to flatten its body into a concave shape to glide between trees when foraging or escaping predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Chrysopelea taprobanica* is oviparous, laying clutches of 4–12 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the pre-monsoon period, often between April and June.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Chrysopelea taprobanica* is endemic to the Indian subcontinent, primarily inhabiting the dry zones of Sri Lanka and localized regions of Peninsular India.
